items.note: SEM plus experimental-versus-control comparison of GAI-supported collaborative music creation with 405 Chinese university students; all named outcomes (creative interest, creative self-efficacy, self-regulated learning, perceived creative competence) are self-reported, though the next stage could check whether the group comparison uses any scored product.

AEA RCT Registry entry only (AEARCTR-0013751): within-subject writing tasks without and with AI, randomized across fixed, piece-rate, and tournament pay, planned 360 participants, outputs scored for originality; registry lists no results or paper, so track for a later version.

Preservice science teachers in Turkey designed analogies with AI (n = 62) or without AI (n = 71); products coded for format, semantic distance, association, and richness via chi-square tests, not rated for creativity, and assignment method is not stated.

21 industrial design students split into AIGC-engaged versus traditional brainstorming groups, ideas rated for novelty, feasibility, correlation, and utility; abstract only partly reachable (Springer page), assignment method not stated, below 50 participants.

Design thinking workshops compared only-human teams with human-AI teams using an AI ideation app; outcomes are idea counts, usability, and novelty; team-level comparison with sample size and assignment not stated in the abstract.

Pre- and post-test experiment (N = 300) on idea generation with versus without AI support, moderated by creative self-efficacy; abstract says AI support enhances creativity but does not say how creativity is measured or how conditions are assigned.

Within-subjects experiment with 75 novice designers on mobile app UI tasks under human-only, AI Overmatch (exposure to superior AI outputs), and XAI-enhanced conditions; outcomes include creative self-efficacy plus originality and idea quality; order randomization not stated.

Architecture students at KFUPM in a GenAI test group versus a control group on a supervised design project, assessed on creativity, time efficiency, and design quality; sample size and assignment not stated in the abstract.

Quasi-experimental pre/post design: 34 interior design students (27 completers) did a manual furniture design and then an AI-assisted redesign in fixed order; outcomes are CSI, NASA-TLX, and expert-juror ratings of designs; no randomization and below 50.

60 engineering students identified design constraints with generative AI or unaided, then all generated concepts without AI (relevant to after_ai); outcomes are constraint and concept counts plus fNIRS brain imaging; assignment not stated and creativity ratings unclear.
